text: Reshuffling every block of seven letters the same way could make the copper's width-7 pattern. Here a reshuffle comes before or after a repeating key on the table.
Reversing each row, places 22 and 29 are carved at 28 and 35 and force M and R in the same slot: that reshuffle with a 7-letter word is dead.
All 5,040 ways of reshuffling seven letters, both orders, key lengths 1 to 52: lengths up to 24 die; 25 and 26 survive as often as on shuffled coppers, and no fragment spells a word.
